lesson_title: The Battery That Taxes Itself: Internal Resistance
hook_text: Your car battery reads 12 volts... then the engine cranks and the headlights dim. The battery just taxed itself.
clip_script: Every battery makes a promise — twelve volts, printed right on the label. But watch what happens when the engine cranks: the headlights sag. Did the promise break? No. The battery paid a tax — to itself. Inside every real battery hides a tiny resistor: the internal resistance. While no current flows, no tax is due, and a voltmeter reads the full promise. But the moment current flows, every ampere pays a toll inside the battery — current times internal resistance — and only what survives reaches the terminals. Now the dimming headlights make sense: the starter motor is a monster of a parallel branch. It opens, the total resistance collapses, the current surges, the internal toll surges with it, and the voltage left over for the lamps sags. Four links: resistance down, current up, toll up, terminal voltage down. That exact chain is worth marks in Paper 1 — and it explains the old torch battery that reads fine on a meter but cannot light a bulb. The promise is still there; the toll has grown monstrous. One hidden resistor, one energy budget: emf equals what the circuit receives plus what the battery keeps. Learn to bill the battery, and the whole topic pays you back.
visual_style: A battery drawn as a bank vault with a toll gate inside; ammeter arrows surging as a starter motor slams open a new lane; headlights sagging, then a graph line drooping from its emf intercept.
mood: Detective energy — exposing the hidden resistor every battery conceals.
pacing: Quick hook on the dimming headlights, steady reveal of the internal toll, four-link chain delivered as rapid beats, confident close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read any battery's secret from one graph.
